reason: The cited evidence does not directly support the key premises. E1 and E2 discuss oxidation in CrFeCoNiMn and general oxide formation but provide no data on Si, no direct comparison of Al vs. Mn diffusion kinetics, and no evidence that Mn oxides are inherently porous or that Al/Si scales are coherent via sluggish diffusion. E3 shows Al improves oxidation resistance at 800 °C in a different alloy system, but does not address Si, diffusion kinetics, or behavior above 900 °C. The premises are largely extrapolated or unsupported by the cited passages.
premises: Al or Si in CrFeCoNiX form dense, low-diffusivity protective oxide layers (Al2O3 or mixed Al–Cr oxide) via sluggish diffusion
Mn in CrFeCoNiX has higher mobility, leading to porous, non-coherent Mn-rich oxides prone to cracking and spallation
Sluggish diffusion of Al/Si limits oxygen ingress and promotes slow-growing, adherent scales above 900 °C
Mn-containing baseline (CrFeCoNiMn) forms unstable, less protective oxide that cracks and spalls above 900 °C
The diffusion kinetics of the substituent element X directly control oxide scale coherence and protective behavior
